title: Basin reserve-web modular colonies
scope: Spatial organization and local resource-sharing topology of the reserve-web vegetation guild in Project Hearthway's initial basin; usable within shared-setting ecology, geography, culture, economy, and story development.
claims: The reserve-web guild's characteristic subsurface networks are organized into bounded modular colony patches.
Each patch contains numerous rooted growth modules connected through a spatially limited living network.
Living connections permit finite local sharing of resources among connected modules.
Damage can sever connections, isolate portions of a patch, and kill modules or sections when sufficiently severe.
Distinct colony patches do not join into one continuous basin-wide organism.
Local resource sharing within a patch does not constitute shared consciousness.
boundaries: The exact number, size, age, shape, density, spacing, depth, and distribution of patches remain undefined.
Module anatomy, individuality, genetic relationship, developmental variation, and an individual module's independent viability remain undefined.
Connection anatomy, carriers, capacity, rate, directionality, losses, regulation, signalling, and failure modes remain undefined.

Threshold-based fragment viability and possible independent-patch stabilization are governed by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-reserve-web-fragment-viability; exact viability thresholds, stabilization timescale, wound response, reconnection, fusion, competition, parasitism, and disease spread remain undefined.
Growth, budding, reproduction, dispersal, dormancy, senescence, succession, and variation among guild members remain undefined.
Primary energy capture, gas exchange, soil, mineral, water, temperature, chemistry, and Mana requirements remain undefined.
No human recognition, terminology, cultivation, harvesting, management, ownership, law, belief, or cultural meaning is established.

Whether and how the System recognizes or appraises a module, patch, species, or guild remains undefined; no personal colony identity, shared level, pooled statistics, Skill, class, reward, or progression lineage is established.
Distinct patches do not form a basin-wide organism, and local resource sharing does not constitute shared consciousness.
The record establishes no ambient spawning, automatic refill, instant long-range transfer, guaranteed recovery, personal colony identity, shared level, or pooled statistics.
story_implications: Physical damage that severs living connections can fragment patches and produce uneven survival and recovery.
Severed sections can create persistent local gaps without causing an automatic basin-wide collapse or reset.
Characters may eventually learn to infer patch condition or boundaries, but no such knowledge or practice is established here.
system_implications: Local resource sharing does not by itself create one personal System actor under CAL0 WLD1.1D.
Any resource transfer requires finite living carriers, capacity, time, compatible matter, and recoverable or irreversible consequences.
Patch growth and recovery follow ordinary causal life cycles under CAL0 WLD2.1A+D rather than spawning or refill behaviour.
research_questions: What anatomical structures distinguish a module, connection, patch boundary, and disconnected section?
What controls patch size, connection density, age, expansion, competition, and spatial distribution?
Which materials move between modules, through what carriers, at what rates, losses, distances, and seasonal conditions?
What exact thresholds, timescales, wound responses, and reconnection conditions determine whether a qualifying isolated fragment stabilizes or fails?
How do patches grow, reproduce, disperse, enter dormancy, senesce, and vary among guild members?
How do grazing, trampling, fire, flood, frost, drought, disease, parasites, and mutualists alter network topology?
Does Mana support any ordinary patch function, and how would its inputs, transformation, capacity, and failures remain causal?
What observations could eventually let local people identify patch boundaries or condition without establishing that knowledge now?
